summary: An essay episode in which Robert Evans draws on anthropology and neuroscience to argue that hierarchy is wired into human brains, that hunter-gatherers actively enforced equality, and that authoritarianism spread like a virus once agriculture and large societies arose.

evidence.note: Host frames the episode as prehistory of authoritarianism rather than a single bastard
Fukuyama essay and 2018 democracy index used to frame present-day backsliding
Egalitarian hunter-gatherer ancestors and prehistoric social organisation
Long segment on Lee's 1970s ox gift and the Ju/'hoansi practice of mocking a hunter's meat
Lee's fieldwork in the Kalahari, modern Botswana
Research on power impairing empathy, tied to social media behaviour of the powerful
Theories of how agriculture, surplus and property let inequality spread
Fascists organising online and fascism as a bottom-up molecular force

notes: Essay episode with no single bastard; deep-dive chosen over meta, though it draws on the show's research. The core period is prehistory (tens of thousands of years ago to early agriculture), below the schema minimum of -5000, so spans are clamped to -5000 and marked approximate. Regions are thin: only the Kalahari fieldwork and Iroquois study get real time.
